standard.title: How Objects Move
standard.description: describe how objects move and how factors including their size, shape or material influence their movement
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior science learning assumed. Students bring everyday experience of moving objects.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe different ways objects move, observe how size, shape and material affect movement, and make comparisons between objects based on how they move.

nodes.label: Objects move in different ways
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can observe and describe different types of object movement (roll, slide, bounce, spin, swing) and group toys or objects by their movement type.
nodes.minimum_width: Students describe at least three different ways objects can move and give one example of each.
nodes.typical_width: Students observe how toys move; describe movement types (roll, slide, bounce, spin); group toys by movement type; describe unusually shaped objects (eggs, tubes) and predict how they might move; and explain what they observe.
wider: Explore how the size and shape of traditional instructive toys used by First Nations Australians influence their movement
Observe and describe ways unusually shaped objects (blocks, tubes, eggs) move when rolled down a slope
Group toys based on their movement and explain the grouping

response_modes.reason: Observing and naming multiple movement types (roll, slide, bounce, spin, swing) across varied objects — including First Nations instructive toys — builds the vocabulary and observation range needed to describe how factors alter movement in Node 2.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations instructive toy direction is elaboration-grounded and culturally rich.
success_criteria: Describes at least three different ways objects can move
Groups at least two objects by movement type and explains the grouping
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 asks students to compare how factors (size, shape, material) affect movement — a comparison that requires movement vocabulary and prior observation of movement types. Students who cannot describe different movement types have no referent for 'how movement changed' when a factor is varied.

nodes.label: Size, shape and material affect how objects move
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare how different-sized, shaped or material objects move and describe at least one factor that affects movement.
nodes.minimum_width: Students compare two objects and describe how one factor (size, shape or material) affects how they move.
nodes.typical_width: Students compare different-sized similar-shaped objects (tennis balls, golf balls, marbles); explore how material affects movement (plastic, foam, cloth, rubber balls); observe how object shape affects rolling or bouncing; and explain the difference they observe.
wider: Compare how different-sized similar-shaped objects (tennis, golf, marble, basketball) roll and bounce
Explore how the material a ball is made from affects movement on a surface
Predict how an unusually shaped object such as an egg or hexagonal block might move down a slope then observe
success_criteria: Compares two objects and describes how at least one factor (size, shape or material) affects how they move
